title: New business accounts, first 60 days
subject: Visigoth Bank, an invented retail bank
source: six owner interviews, three call transcripts, a ticket export and one usage table, all invented

records.title: Interview: mobile dog groomer
records.takeaway: Her first large card payment was held for four days and she paid a supplier from her personal account.

records.title: Interview: two-person joinery
records.takeaway: They still invoice from a spreadsheet because they could not tell which invoices had been paid.

records.title: Interview: market food stall
records.takeaway: Stopped using the account after a held payment, went back to the old bank.

records.title: Interview: freelance bookkeeper
records.takeaway: Happy overall. Wants her accountant to see the account without sharing her login.

records.title: Interview: cafe owner
records.takeaway: The second director waited 19 days to get access.

records.title: Interview: electrician
records.takeaway: Cannot tell business spending from personal on the same card statement view.

records.title: Support calls: three held-payment calls
records.takeaway: In all three the agent could not say when the money would be released.

records.title: Ticket export, last 90 days
records.takeaway: Held or reversed payments are 30% of tickets, the largest topic.

records.title: Activity by day since opening
records.takeaway: 17% of accounts have no activity by day 60. Most of the drop is between days 10 and 25.

records.title: My first big payment gets held and nobody can tell me when I will get it
records.who: Sole traders who take card payments
records.situation: The first or second payment well above their usual size, in the first month
records.today: They pay suppliers from personal money, phone support repeatedly, and some move back to their previous bank.

evidence.quote: Four days. I had the food bill for the week due and the money was just sitting there with a little padlock on it.
I rang three times. Each person said it was under review. Review of what? I sold forty lunches.
I understand, but I am not able to see a release date on my side.
96 of 318 tickets (30%) concern a held or reversed payment.

against.quote: I had one held early on. It cleared the next morning, it did not bother me.

records.measure: 41% of accounts that raise a held-payment ticket in their first 30 days are inactive by day 60, against 17% overall (Support Insights, S-8 with S-9).
records.unknown: Why payments are held, and whether the hold itself or not knowing the release date is what drives people away. No source includes the risk team's rules.

records.title: I cannot tell which of my invoices have been paid
records.today: They keep a spreadsheet and tick off payments by reading the transaction list.

evidence.quote: Money comes in with a reference like 'INV' and half a surname. I match them up on a Sunday night.
For my clients this is the number one thing. They do not know who owes them.

against.quote: Accounts that receive bank transfers are no more likely to go inactive than the average.

records.unknown: How many new accounts invoice at all. The usage table does not separate transfers that pay invoices from other transfers.

records.title: My business partner cannot get into our own account for weeks
records.situation: Right after opening, while the second person is being verified
records.today: One person does all the banking, or they share a login.

evidence.quote: Nineteen days. I counted. She is a director of the company and she could not see the balance.
We just both use my phone. I know we are not meant to.

records.unknown: How long verification of a second person takes in general. Two interviews are not a measurement.

records.title: I cannot separate what I spent on the business from what I spent on myself
records.who: Sole traders using one card for everything
records.today: They go through statements by hand.
records.return_note: One electrician is not enough. Is there anything in the tickets about this?

evidence.quote: It is all one list. Van fuel, my kid's trainers, all of it.

against.quote: 4 of 318 tickets mention categories or tax.

records.unknown: Whether this is a banking problem or a bookkeeping habit.

records.title: I want my accountant to see my account without having my login
records.today: They export statements and email them.
records.park_note: Real, but nothing suggests it makes people leave in the first 60 days.

evidence.quote: I would pay for read-only access for my accountant tomorrow.

records.title: My card reader took two weeks to arrive and I could not trade properly
records.who: Businesses that ordered a card reader at opening
records.situation: The gap between opening and delivery
records.today: They take cash or use a competitor's reader.

evidence.quote: 51 of 318 tickets concern card or reader delivery.
